assumptions: Simulation time 00:15 corresponds to 07:00 after a 15-minute warmup.
Mainline inlet uses station 400790 at at least 80% reported coverage; comparison targets retain at least 90% coverage.
The existing motorway buffer is about 1 km upstream of the M2 analysis start; omitted upstream exits and inlet imputation are uncertainties.
PeMS five-minute flow is multiplied by 12 to obtain vehicles per hour.
Measured Mathilda exit demand is removed from the through flow; measured Mathilda, Moffett, and San Antonio entrances are injected on audited edges.
Missing-entrance groups are assumed demand, and other omitted ramps remain unknown.
PeMS speed is a comparison target and is not imposed on vehicles.
Mainline routes follow ordered motorway checkpoints; passengers in managed lanes are assumed eligible or toll-paying.
Human behavior uses stochastic Krauss following and the default lane-changing model.
additional_assumptions: Station 400790 with at least 80% reported coverage supplies an inlet proxy; comparison targets retain 90% coverage.
The 1.008 km existing motorway buffer precedes the M2 analysis start. Its flow may include omitted upstream exits; its exact lane paint is not certified.
Measured speed is not imposed on vehicles; the buffer tests whether the prior inlet suppressed upstream congestion.

estimated_ramp_mappings.name: Unmeasured post-Shoreline net-exit group at a San Antonio exit
estimated_ramp_mappings.basis: Calibration-only hypothesis: 8041 veh/h at 401507 plus 560 measured San Antonio entrance minus 5616 across four 402377 channels leaves 2985 before the missing lane. An assumed 1500 veh/h missing-lane contribution gives a rounded 1500 veh/h net-exit group. Gross ramp flows and field wiring remain unknown.

window_exit_vehicles: arrivals in window, all modeled exits
cohort_completed_vehicles: window departures completed by run end
cohort_unfinished_vehicles: window departures unfinished at run end
cohort_mean_time_loss_seconds: completed departure cohort, mean SUMO timeLoss
trajectory_timesteps: all expected window timesteps including empty
stopped_vehicle_seconds: sum stopped counts times sample period
mean_ramp_stopped_vehicles: time mean on entrance approach edges
peak_ramp_stopped_vehicles: time maximum on entrance approach edges
mean_timestep_speed_mph: mean of nonempty timestep mean speeds
temporal_mean_speed_stddev_mph: population stddev of timestep mean speeds
mean_squared_acceleration_m2_per_s4: mean a squared over vehicle samples
rms_acceleration_m_per_s2: square root of mean squared acceleration
whole_run_mean_depart_delay_seconds: all inserted trips mean insertion delay
whole_run_max_depart_delay_seconds: all inserted trips maximum insertion delay
peak_insertion_backlog_vehicles: maximum waiting to insert, whole run
window_peak_insertion_backlog_vehicles: maximum waiting to insert in window

limitations: M3 held-out fidelity remains limited: October 15 missed both flow and speed targets; combined held-out speed MAE was 14.90 mph. M4 instrumentation does not revalidate H0.
Seed spread describes stochastic simulation variation, not total model uncertainty.
Trajectory scope includes modeled ramps, upstream buffer, and internal junction links.
Queues are stopped-vehicle count proxies, not contiguous queue lengths in meters. Entrance counts omit internal junction links and vehicles waiting to insert.
Temporal variability of domain mean speed depends on demand and spatial composition; it does not establish wave stability or disturbance recovery.
Acceleration squared is a smoothness proxy, not energy or fuel use. FCD speed and acceleration use SUMO's default two-decimal output precision.

CACC is a conservative passenger overlay with ideal acceleration messages and native Krauss safety constraints; 1.5 s headway is retained. Trucks are human driven. Policy comparisons do not establish real-world safety or string stability.
Unknown gross ramp movements and the annual truck proxy remain M3 assumptions.
